Mitesh: noticed a perf delta after the kernel-selection tweak in main (hash 9f3b2d). Chat workloads hit-rate for prefix KV cache dropped ~82% -> ~56% on canary. completions seem fine. anyone else see this?
Sara: ouch. which change specifically? the seq_len_bucket switch? :face_with_monocle:
Mitesh: yeah that + we started selecting fused-attn kernel for seq<=256 if packed. suspect interaction with how we serialize KV keys (we key by model+seq_bucket+prefix_hash currently).
Oliver: can reproduce locally with chat-replay profile. attaching short stack log:
```
flamegraph: runtime::attn_fused -> runtime::kv_write -> hashing::xxh3
90% in fused kernel path for short seq
KV write latency spikes 3x for hits
```
Janet: wow. so hits are now slower not just misses? that points to eviction/compaction churn or different KV layout serialized by kernel path.
Mitesh: my profiler shows more frequent partial-evictions on the LRU ring for small-seq bucked entries. probably because packed kernels write smaller slices that collide in our chunk allocator.
Sara: does the cache key include tokenization normalization? RAG retrievals often have small whitespace/metadata differences. if kernel changes how we chunk, two semantically identical prefixes might map differently.
Mitesh: we key on raw prompt string + model + seq_bucket. tokenizer differences shouldn't matter here, but structured outputs with trailing JSON braces were causing inconsistent whitespace on some test prompts. that could lower hit-rate.
Oliver: short repro script:
```
// toy key normalization
function normalizeKey(prompt){
  return prompt.replace(/\s+/g,' ').trim().slice(0,1024)
}
```
maybe strip retrieval metadata like `source:` fields before hashing.
Janet: I ran a workload split: chat-with-RAG vs plain-completions. RAG chat hit-rate dropped 78->50, plain completions 85->82. So RAG is disproportionately affected.
Mitesh: hypothesis: retrieval prefixes contain variable doc ids and annotations -> large key cardinality -> more small entries -> higher eviction pressure in the small-seq bucket. plus fused kernel writes make chunk alignment different, causing more GC in chunk allocator.
Sara: mitigation ideas: 1) normalize/strip retrieval metadata before keying 2) increase small-seq pool capacity 3) pre-warm KV for active conversations during canary rollout 4) revert kernel change?
Oliver: pre-warm idea: integrate a canary prefetcher that runs synthetic prefixes for top N customers after deploy so rings get warmed. simple script: `for convo in top_convos: call(prompt_prefix(convo))`
Janet: also consider adding a stable key suffix: conversation-id + prefix-hash instead of raw prefix string. that reduces key length variance.
Mitesh: agree. quick patch plan: a) add key normalization to strip `^\[source:.*?\]` style blocks b) increase small-seq slab by +25% as an emergency canary config c) add prefetch hook to rollout playbook.
Sara: can we quantify cost of increasing slab? ops-impacted?
Janet: rough calc: +25% small-seq memory -> +8% overall GPU memory used on average, cost hit modest. tradeoff: hit-rate up -> fewer token compute.
Mitesh: I'm pushing a WIP PR with normalization and slab toggle: PR #4126. running unit + perf tests.
deploy-bot: canary deploy queued for service/inference-runtime sha=9f3b2d -> scheduled 10:30 UTC. monitor kv-hit-rate dashboards.
Oliver: after applying normalization locally, hit-rate on sample RAG trace moved 52->70. still below original 82 but big improvement.
Sara: nice. let's also add a short-term metric in alerting: if chat-kv-hit-rate drops >15% in 10m during rollout, auto-rollback.
Mitesh: agreed. I'll add the alert and the prefetch hook to the rollout playbook. planning to keep kernel selection change but with allocator fix next week.
Janet: add a note to changelog + incident-channel ping if canary hit-rate dips.
Mitesh: thanks all — will update PR and post results here once canary finishes.
Oliver: thumbs up, will help verify heatmaps and flamegraphs post-deploy.
Sara: if anyone hits a repro I can help instrument token-level traces to see exact key variance.
Mitesh: copying results here when done. :rocket:
